# components

**In one sentence:** The pieces of the Caption Verifier screen: the modal frame, the caption editor, the source-vs-rendered preview pane, and the filmstrip of thumbnails.

## Why it exists
The Caption Verifier checks whether an image model understands a caption. It renders a new image from the caption and shows it next to the original photo. Each part of that screen lives in its own file here. `../caption_verify.js` puts them together.

## What's inside
| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `modal.js` | `captionVerifyModal(itemCount, settings)` builds the empty modal in three rows: a header with the count, progress and model id, then a workspace (editor beside preview), then the filmstrip with prev/next buttons. |
| `editor.js` | `createCaptionEditor(panel, { onInput, onVerdict })` builds one textarea and three verdict buttons. It is built once, and `show(item, view)` swaps the content when the selection changes, so focus is kept. It also has `syncVerdict`, `syncCounts` (character count, plus token count once a render exists) and a slot for the model-load status. |
| `preview.js` | `renderCaptionPreview` draws the source image, the rendered image, render settings (seed, steps, guidance, size, time), the "Render" and "Re-roll seed" buttons, and notices (caption edited since render, caption truncated at the encoder limit, errors). `setPreviewStale` and `setPreviewWaitLabel` update small parts without rebuilding the pane. `waitLabel` turns the job phase into "Preparing model…", "Loading model…" or "Rendering…". |
| `strip.js` | `captionVerifyTile` makes one filmstrip tile on top of the shared `components/review_card.js`: click selects, right-click cycles the verdict. `syncCaptionVerifyTiles` marks tiles as reviewed or edited. |

## How it works
- The modal frame comes first. Then the editor fills `.caption-verify-editor`, the preview fills `.caption-verify-preview` and the tiles fill `#captionVerifyTiles`.
- While a render is running, the preview pane disables its buttons. If the running render belongs to another image, it says which one ("one render at a time").
- Typing and the one-second timer only update small parts of the pane, so the two `<img>` tags are not reloaded over and over.

## Who uses it
- `../caption_verify.js`: the only importer.
- Shared code it uses: `static/core/dom.js` (`escapeText`), `static/caption/status.js` (`formatElapsed`), `static/components/review_card.js`.
- Tests: `tests/ui/static/caption_verify.test.js`.

## Good to know
- `waitLabel` is exported but only used inside `preview.js`.
